s: The world's most-deployed open-source OLTP relational database - boring, mature, everywhere.
w: InnoDB engine provides ACID via redo log + MVCC row versioning. B+tree indexes serve point/range lookups; buffer pool keeps hot pages in RAM. Replication is primary-replica via binlog (async by default, semi-sync optional). Query optimizer chooses plans from statistics; performance schema exposes internals.
use: Standard transactional workloads: users, orders, inventory with joins
Read-heavy products served by replica pools (feeds, catalogs, CMS)
Teams wanting ubiquitous tooling/hiring pool and predictable operations
Moderate write rates (<~2-5k durable writes/sec vertical) before sharding talk
avoid: Write-throughput ceilings beyond vertical scale (then cassandra/dynamodb/sharded stacks)
Schemaless document chaos (mongodb fits flexible docs better)

pat.d: Writes to primary, heavy analytics-ish reads to replicas.
Horizontal split by tenant/user-id with a routing layer.

pits: Replica lag surprises UX ('my edit vanished') - route read-your-writes to primary or use semi-sync
Lock contention on hot rows - shorten transactions, add idempotency, consider queues for hot counters
Connection count ceilings - proxy with PgBouncer-analog (ProxySQL) pooling
tips: Capacity framing: reads scale with replicas, writes hit one primary - know YOUR ratio
Sharding narrative: pick shard key = highest-cardinality access dimension (user_id); rebalancing pain justifies managed solutions
